findings.claim: EnumTemplate.tt uses an inverted guard (`#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK`), while every other template uses `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. As a result, generated enum formatters get no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on net5+/netcoreapp targets, which are exactly the targets where the change intends to emit it. This breaks 'All generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage' for enum formatters. The 222 regenerated snapshots would bake this in rather than catch it.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ExcludeFromCodeCoverageGapTests.EnumFormatter_IsExcludedFromCodeCoverage. It compiles an enum member of a [MessagePackObject] with no preprocessor symbols and asserts that the generated IMessagePackFormatter<MyEnum> class carries System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. On head the attribute sits in an inactive #if region, so the test fails.

findings.claim: The attribute is suppressed for consumers compiling for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and is allowed on classes. The derived criterion only permits conditional emission where the attribute does not exist, so for all those consumers no generated code is decorated. The README addition states the false premise that the attribute is unavailable there.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ExcludeFromCodeCoverageGapTests.Formatter_IsExcludedFromCodeCoverage_WhenTargetingNetStandard20. It parses the user source and the generated source with preprocessor symbol NETSTANDARD2_0 and asserts the generated MyObject formatter carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute; it fails on head. The same guard appears in ResolverTemplate.tt, CompositeResolverTemplate.tt, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt and README.md:1640.

findings.claim: The resolver template now unconditionally adds [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to the user's own `partial class` declared with [GeneratedMessagePackResolver]. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has AllowMultiple=false. A user who already decorated their resolver partial with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage], which is a natural workaround for this very issue, now gets CS0579 (duplicate attribute) and code that compiled on base breaks. There is no setting to opt out.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ExcludeFromCodeCoverageGapTests.UserAttributedResolver_StillCompiles. The user source declares `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage][GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class MyResolver`. The test asserts the post-generation compilation has no errors; on head it reports CS0579.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always-on, no setting. Every template (Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Enum, Union, Resolver incl. FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper, CompositeResolver) unconditionally emits [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on its generated types. Users cannot turn it off.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Same emission, but on by default with an opt-out setting, which the requirement explicitly calls acceptable. Add a boolean generator option (e.g. a property on GeneratorOptions/FormattersOptions read from an MSBuild/analyzer-config property such as MessagePackExcludeFromCodeCoverage=false). Thread it into each template's context and wrap the emitted attribute lines in a `<# if (Options.EmitExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #> ... <# } #>` check. Default true, so existing snapshots are unchanged.
